title: Administrator guide
intro: The administrator app is a local workspace for provider configuration, diagnostic ingestion and evidence review. It is not a public service with production-grade operator authentication.

sections.title: What the administrator workspace is for
paragraphs: The MelliAtlas administrator workspace supports operators who configure sources and inspect the quality of information shown on the beekeeper map. The goal is not merely to download records from another service: the application must preserve provenance, expose possible errors and allow a person to review uncertain evidence. The public map and the administrator workspace share the backend and PostGIS storage, but serve different purposes. One is for reading geographic information; the other is for managing its collection and review.

The workflow starts with a provider configuration: endpoint, HTTP method, regional parameters and access constraints. Saving those settings does not automatically fetch any records. For diagnostics, an operator can currently request one page at a time; this is a temporary development feature, not a complete district synchronization process. The backend preserves source material, parsed observations and ingestion history so that operators can understand where a field record came from and why it is visible or excluded.

The preview map lets you select a polygon and inspect its details in a persistent sidebar. Even a successfully imported record may contain incomplete or incorrect geometry, dates or product names. Mark evidence as verified only after comparing it with an accessible original source and documenting the reason for the decision. Pending means the operator review is not complete; rejected records must not appear on the public map. Evidence review is not a scientific assessment of whether a pesticide is safe for bees.

An isolated local DEMO database is available for learning and interface testing. It contains fictional parcels, products and review states, makes no Saturn requests and must not be mixed with real evidence. Automated district synchronization with a shared 24-hour cache is still disabled until the actual upstream district-filter contract is verified. The sections below describe current operator tasks, temporary controls, review steps and troubleshooting. Because the administrator API does not yet have production-grade internet authentication, keep this workspace local.

sections.title: 1. Find your way around
paragraphs: Data collection shows ingestion status and a preview map; Sources lists the registry; Configuration edits the provider connection; Record review shows candidates awaiting a decision. Help contains this guide.
Question-mark controls beside technical fields display explanations. Click again, click outside, or press Escape to dismiss them.

sections.title: 2. Development-only page retrieval
paragraphs: Fetch next page is a diagnostic action retained during development. It fetches one bounded provider page and saves valid candidates. Next page is a technical cursor, not a district identifier.
The source-wide throttle reserves request starts at least 65 seconds apart. A quick repeat may produce SOURCE_THROTTLED. One page is not evidence of complete district coverage.
steps: Open Data collection and check the provider configuration state.
Use Fetch next page only when an intentional diagnostic import is needed.
Inspect received and saved candidate counts, the next page number and last run status.
Review the preview map and underlying evidence before operator decisions.
notes: Use the isolated DEMO database for UI walkthroughs; it makes no live Saturn calls.

sections.title: 3. Preview map and details sidebar
paragraphs: Technically valid source polygons appear with review-specific styles. Unreviewed records use dashed outlines; operator-reviewed records use solid outlines. Rejected records should not be published.
Selecting a polygon shows the organization, separate parcel markers, dates, products, crop, review status, source URL and retrieval timestamp in a persistent sidebar. No Leaflet popup is opened.
steps: Select a polygon to show its corresponding details on the right.
Compare the source claims against the original record where accessible.
Close the sidebar or select another polygon to compare records.

sections.title: 4. Operator evidence review
paragraphs: Record review lists candidates awaiting a decision. Verify against primary evidence, not just map geometry. A reviewer name and an evidence note of at least 20 characters are required.
Verify and publish requires a valid geometry and a valid review form. Rejection also requires a written explanation. A saved decision changes the record status or visibility in the public map.
steps: Open the original source link, if available, and compare the key facts.
Enter your reviewer name and an evidence-specific note.
Verify or reject only after sufficient source review.
Confirm the updated status in the list and map after refresh.
notes: Operator review does not establish whether a pesticide application is safe for bees.

sections.title: 5. Provider configuration
paragraphs: Configuration can edit the HTTPS endpoint, HTTP method, region code, filter container and JSON request parameters. Saving only stores settings; it does NOT fetch provider data.
Provider-specific region identifiers may differ from official region codes. Do not invent unverified district or date parameters for Saturn.
steps: Inspect current settings and revision.
Change only fields supported by a verified request contract and access policy.
Save and confirm that no collection was started.
On revision conflict, reload and reconcile the operator changes.

sections.title: 6. Source registry and provenance
paragraphs: Sources lists registered names, URLs and terms review status. Stored records retain provider attribution and original URLs.
Technical parsing and unreviewed publication terms do not grant permission to redistribute source information publicly.

sections.title: 7. District cache — planned
paragraphs: The intended workflow selects a verified district and period, then refreshes a shared cache. The 24-hour TTL is counted only after all required pages finish successfully. Partial work and failures do not extend freshness.
Refresh district now remains disabled because the real Saturn district/date filter contract is unverified. Do not substitute a viewport rectangle or restart a full-region scan as a workaround.
notes: District refresh is planned functionality, not a currently available live-data update.

sections.title: 8. Troubleshooting
paragraphs: No fields: check DB availability, ingestion status and valid geometry. Missing polygons never demonstrate there were no treatments.
SOURCE_THROTTLED: respect provider pacing; avoid rapid retries. For ingestion errors, inspect sanitized API diagnostics rather than exporting private provider records.
If help overlays the UI, click outside it or press Escape. If DEMO records are missing, confirm pnpm demo:dev is using a prepared demo database.

example.title: Walkthrough using fictional data
paragraphs: The isolated DEMO dataset contains 12 synthetic observations: four simulated verified, seven pending, one rejected, and one without geometry. Ten polygons are eligible for the public map.
DEMO agricultural cooperative 02 and DEMO-PARCEL-02 are fictional labels. Source links end in .invalid and never refer to real Saturn plans.
steps: Run pnpm demo:prepare and pnpm demo:dev at the repository root.
Open Admin at http://127.0.0.1:5174 and select a DEMO polygon.
Inspect the review status, products and parcel marker in the sidebar.
Open Record review to explore the workflow without treating sample evidence as real.
For an isolated automated check, stop dev servers and run pnpm e2e:demo.
notes: DEMO is for interface testing only. It is not real cadastral evidence, spraying data or Saturn information.

warnings: The local administrator has no production-grade server authentication yet.
Do not expose Admin or /api/v1/operator/* through a public reverse proxy.
Never treat DEMO records as Saturn information or verify them as real evidence.
Operator review is about evidence provenance, not a bee-safety assessment.
